Mental Health Care Plan

Patient & GP Details
- Patient: Jack Armani, DOB: 12/08/1958, Gender: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded, Address: Not recorded
- Referring GP: Dr Deen Mirza, Practice: GP at Hand, Practice Address: Not recorded. Provider No.: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded

Clinical Assessment

Identified Problems/Provisional Diagnoses:
- Principal: Acute neurological event — suspected acute ischemic stroke (right hemispheric distribution) (supported by transcript and DDx; likelihood: High)
- Secondary: Intracerebral hemorrhage (right-sided) (DDx consistent; likelihood: Medium)
- Tertiary: Focal seizure with post-ictal (Todd's) paresis (DDx considered; likelihood: Medium–Low)

Clinical Details & History:
- Medications: Metformin; Losartan; Amlodipine. (dose/route/frequency not documented)
- Allergies/ADRs: Penicillin
- Past Medical History: Type 2 diabetes mellitus; Hypertension

Mental Health History:
- Previous Diagnoses: Not recorded
- Past Treatments (Therapy, Medications, Hospitalizations): Not recorded
- Family History: Father with heart disease; no psychiatric family history recorded

Social & Lifestyle Factors:
- Living Situation: Lives alone
- Social Support: Not recorded (no one at home at time of call)
- Occupation/Education: Not recorded
- Alcohol Use: Drinks beers; "a few" over weekend and "a couple" during the week
- Smoking/Substance Use: Ex-smoker
- Key Stressors: Not recorded

Mental Status Examination (MSE):
- Appearance & General Behaviour: Telephone consult; patient alert, cooperative; concerned/anxious
- Mood & Affect: Worried/anxious (patient repeatedly asked if this was something to worry about)
- Speech & Thought: Speech described by patient as slower/harder; increased effort required to speak (patient-reported dysarthria). Thought processes coherent on telephone.
- Perception: Left-sided facial tingling (patient-reported). No hallucinations recorded.

Cognition:
- Orientation: Oriented to self and DOB provided
- Attention/Concentration: Able to engage in conversation; some speech slowing reported
- Memory: Not recorded
- Insight & Judgement: Recognizes problem and agrees to ambulance; demonstrates appropriate help-seeking behaviour

Physical Symptoms:
- Sleep: Symptoms began on awakening this morning; no awkward sleep position reported
- Appetite: Not recorded
- Motivation/Energy: Not recorded
- Anxiety Symptoms: Expressed worry and concern about symptoms; anxious about severity

Risk Assessment:
- Suicidal/Self-Harm/Risk to Others: Not recorded
- Protective Factors: Ambulance called and en route; clinician stayed on line and provided instructions; patient able to follow instructions
- Overall Current Risk Level (Self): High medical risk due to suspected acute stroke (emergency ambulance activated)
- Emergency Contact: Not recorded

Formulation:
- Predisposing factors: Older age with vascular risk factors (hypertension, type 2 diabetes).
- Precipitating factor: Sudden onset of focal neurological deficits on awakening (~1 hour prior to call).
- Perpetuating factors: Lives alone (may delay access to immediate help); no witnessed neurological exam available due to telephone assessment.
- Protective factors: Prompt recognition by GP, ambulance alerted, clinician remained on line and provided clear instructions.
- Integration: Patient presents with acute focal neurological symptoms (complete left arm paralysis per patient report, left facial tingling, dysarthria, dysphagia) consistent with a central vascular event (acute right hemispheric ischemic stroke most likely per DDx). Emergency hospital assessment (imaging, stroke team) is required to confirm diagnosis and initiate treatment. Secondary considerations include intracerebral hemorrhage and focal seizure with post-ictal paresis; differentiation requires in-person evaluation, vital signs and imaging.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Immediate: Safe transfer to hospital for urgent assessment and treatment.
  - Short-term: Stabilisation and clarification of diagnosis in ED.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Ensure timely ambulance attendance and rapid access to stroke services/CT brain to distinguish ischemic vs hemorrhagic stroke and enable appropriate acute treatment.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Leave front door unlocked and sit in hallway by front door for ambulance access (patient agreed and proceeded to door).
  - Remain on the line with clinician until ambulance arrival (as arranged).
  - Present to ED for assessment and imaging as transported by ambulance.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Ambulance called and arranged to attend patient’s home (documented in transcript).
  - Provide pre-hospital instructions (stay by door, keep door unlocked); remained on the telephone line until ambulance arrival.
  - Recommend urgent hospital triage to stroke team for CT brain and acute stroke pathway (implied by clinician statements).
  - Document medications and allergies for handover to ambulance/ED.

Secondary Problem (Anxiety/worry related to acute medical event):
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduce acute anxiety and receive clear information and reassurance during emergency transfer.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Provide timely reassurance, clear instructions and appropriate handover to ED; arrange follow-up for emotional support if needed post-acute care.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Use breathing/grounding techniques if feeling panicked (patient not specifically instructed in transcript; patient to ask staff in ED for support).
  - Accept assistance and information from ambulance/ED staff.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide reassurance on phone (clinician expressed concern and reassurance that ambulance/ED will manage).
  - Ensure ED handover includes note of patient anxiety and living situation (lives alone) to inform discharge planning and support needs.
  - Recommend consideration of post-discharge follow-up for psychological distress (Not recorded whether arranged; clinician to facilitate if needed).

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered:
  - Explanation that symptoms may represent a stroke and require emergency hospital assessment.
  - Ambulance arranged; instructions: leave front door unlocked and sit in hallway by front door; wait for ambulance.
  - Explanation of expected ED pathway (assessment by stroke team, possible treatments).
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - Not recorded (acute event managed as emergency; patient instructed to await ambulance).
- Coping Strategies:
  - Reassurance provided; clinician remained on line. No specific coping strategies beyond instructions recorded.

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Patient verbally agreed to ambulance attendance and to follow instructions (documented).
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Dr Deen Mirza is the consulting GP; plan completed by treating clinician in call.
- Review Date: Not recorded

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Acute ischemic stroke (right hemispheric — MCA cortical or lacunar/internal capsule infarct)
  - Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Sudden-onset unilateral left arm paralysis, ipsilateral facial sensory change, dysarthria/dysphagia on waking in a patient with vascular risk factors (hypertension, T2DM).
- Intracerebral hemorrhage (right-sided)
  - Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: Hypertension is a risk factor and hemorrhage can present acutely with focal deficits; requires imaging to differentiate.
- Focal seizure with post-ictal (Todd's) paralysis
  - Likelihood: Medium–Low
  - Justification: Transient post-ictal weakness can present similarly; no witnessed seizure or post-ictal confusion reported, making this less likely than stroke.

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Objective neurological examination findings (facial asymmetry, limb power, cranial nerve exam) — not available due to telephone consult.
  - Vital signs (blood pressure, glucose) — not recorded.
  - Imaging/laboratory results — not available.
  - Contact details, address confirmation for ambulance (address presumed provided to ambulance but not documented in transcript).
  - Formal mental health history and prior psychiatric diagnoses — not recorded.
  - Follow-up plan post-hospital discharge regarding psychosocial support — not recorded.
● Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - None noted. Transcript reports focal neurological deficits and DDx ranks stroke as high likelihood; both consistent.
● Transcript quality notes:
  - Telephone consultation — no visual assessment possible.
  - Dialogue complete for emergency call; some brief pauses and overlapping talk but adequate for documented events.
  - No objective exam or vitals documented; all focal findings are patient-reported.
